subject: Pricing ladder and feature cascade — packaging options & stepdown path

Subject: Packaging options for pilot → scale (pricing ladder brainstorm)

Hi Aditi —

Great to chat this morning. Per our call, I wanted to outline two packaging paths that let Medimetrics start with a pilot footprint and then scale predictably without renegotiating core entitlements each time you hit a new usage tier. High level: a pricing "ladder" (throughput-first tiers with credit top-ups) vs a "feature cascade" (modular feature bundles that can be toggled during rollout).

Quick asks from your side: which one is higher priority — minimizing upfront cost during pilot, or preserving feature parity as you grow? Also, you mentioned procurement will want a clear stepdown/rollback path if usage drops.

I can put together a short one-pager + recommended SOW language for both. Ben and Lauren copied here to confirm feasibility and any SLA/credit implications.

Action: I’ll send a written options matrix by EOD tomorrow and a draft SOW for procurement to review.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — this is helpful. Priorities:
- Pilot cost needs to be small (proof of concept with 3 teams),
- Production feature parity is important for two of our apps (Clinical Search, Prior Auth),
- Procurement wants a 60-day rollback/stepdown with defined credits if we overcommit.

Can you show:
1) A ladder approach where we buy an initial throughput block and can top up credits monthly, with pre-defined stepdown credits if we reduce commit within 60 days;
2) A cascade bundle where features are grouped (Core, Clinical, Integrations) and we can flip off Integrations if we need to reallocate spend.

Also, we’ll need a simple price anchor for enterprise support and 99.9% SLA.

If you can send an options matrix + SOW draft for procurement that calls out the stepdown math, procurement will take a look next week.

— Aditi

Ben / Lauren —
Forwarding Aditi's priorities. Procurement will require explicit stepdown credit math (60-day guardrail). Can you validate that the ladder top-up model (monthly credit purchases with auto-apply) can be backstopped with a 60-day financial stepdown and still keep our unit economics within acceptable bounds?

Specifics we need to confirm:
- Stepdown formula proposal: refund X% of committed monthly base for each month remaining in the commit window (e.g., 50% for months >30 and <=60). Need the modeled impact on ARR and expected credit liability.
- For feature cascade: confirm which subfeatures should be gated per bundle (Core, Clinical, Integrations), and whether Integrations toggled off can simply reduce the reported seat/throughput equivalent.

I’ll include whatever you give me in the options matrix for procurement. Goal: a clean SOW appendix that procurement can sign off without legal needing a full renegotiation.

Thanks — Sean

Hi Aditi —

Attached are two artifacts: 1) a one-page options matrix (Redwood_Pricing_Ladder_v2.pdf) showing the ladder vs cascade with concrete pricing examples for your pilot and a scaled commit, and 2) a draft SOW appendix (SOW_Medimetrics_draft.docx) that calls out the 60-day stepdown math and credit flow. Highlights:

- Ladder (recommended for throughput predictability): buy an initial monthly throughput block (Block A) sized for pilot. Monthly top-ups are at 75% of the unit price of the next full tier. Stepdown: if you reduce base commit within 60 days, we issue credits equal to 50% of the remaining commit value for months 31-60 and 25% for months >60 (language in appendix).

- Feature cascade (recommended if feature gating matters): bundles are Core / Clinical / Integrations. Turning Integrations off during a stepdown reduces billable throughput by an estimated 15–20% (we model reduction per integration connector in the appendix).

- SLA & support: enterprise support add-on is a flat monthly fee in the SOW; 99.9% uptime credit language included.

Next steps: procurement review → send back redlines by Tue 11th if possible. If procurement signs off on the stepdown math, we can freeze pricing and move to DocuSign. I included HubSpot and DocuSign links in this thread for tracking.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Ladder_v2.pdf (summary), SOW_Medimetrics_draft.docx (appendix + stepdown language).

Best,

2) On stepdown: can you soften the months 31–60 band to 40% instead of 50%? Procurement says 50% is a blocker for their internal approval.

If you can confirm those two items and send an updated SOW (one-page redline), we should be in shape to issue an initial PO next week.
